title: The G7 Has Opened in Evian. Iran, Trade, and India's Seat at the Table Are All in Play.
excerpt: Modi arrives at the French lakeside summit with a dense agenda: the Iran peace deal, a Trump bilateral on Wednesday, and the visa question that won't go away.
body:
The G7 summit opened in Evian-les-Bains on Monday under the long shadow of the United States' newly announced peace deal with Iran — a framework agreement that has already sent oil prices sliding and global markets rising, and which now dominates the diplomatic agenda on the shores of Lake Geneva.

French President Emmanuel Macron greeted world leaders at the lakeside resort for what serves as both a diplomatic capstone for his second and final term in office and an attempt to forge consensus on an unusually crowded docket: Iran, Ukraine, China's industrial overcapacity, and critical mineral supply chains.

India, alongside Brazil, Kenya and South Korea, has been invited to join the G7 discussions — a seat at the table that New Delhi has used in recent years to position itself as the voice of the Global South. For Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who is on the second leg of a six-day tour of France and Slovakia, the summit offers a chance to address three issues of direct consequence to the Indian diaspora: trade, energy prices, and visa policy.

## The Iran Deal Looms Over Everything

Hours before the summit opened, U.S. President Donald Trump declared on Truth Social that "the Deal with the Islamic Republic of Iran is now complete." Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, whose country mediated the talks, confirmed an "immediate and permanent termination of military operations on all fronts, including in Lebanon." The memorandum of understanding is scheduled to be formally signed in Switzerland on Friday.

The deal calls for the immediate reopening of the Strait of Hormuz — a chokepoint through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil supply has historically flowed — and the lifting of the U.S. naval blockade on Iranian ports. In exchange, Tehran has committed to maintaining its nuclear status quo during a 60-day ceasefire period, during which a broader agreement on sanctions relief, enriched uranium stockpiles, and Iran's nuclear future will be negotiated.

For India, the third-largest oil importer in the world, the implications are immediate. Brent crude dived 4.5 per cent to $83.40 a barrel on Monday morning, its lowest level in more than three months. Indian bond yields fell and the rupee surged past the highs set after the Reserve Bank of India's June 5 policy measures.

## Modi-Trump Bilateral Set for Wednesday

Modi and Trump are scheduled to meet on the sidelines of the summit on Wednesday — their first face-to-face encounter in 16 months. The agenda is dense. A U.S. senior official said trade would be a central topic, with Washington pushing for "a very good deal" while noting that no agreement would be closed at the G7. U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer will travel to India the following week for further negotiations, with both sides eyeing a first tranche of a bilateral trade agreement by mid-July.

But the trade talks are only one layer. Indian officials have said the meeting would also cover H-1B visas — a lifeline for hundreds of thousands of Indian tech workers in the United States — and energy cooperation, potentially including Indian purchases of Venezuelan oil. The killing of three Indian sailors in U.S. Navy strikes in the Strait of Hormuz, which prompted Delhi to summon the American envoy twice, remains a source of friction.

## Anti-G7 Protests Erupt in Geneva

Across the border in Geneva, up to 7,000 people marched against the summit on Sunday in a largely peaceful protest that turned violent in places. Demonstrators set fire to a Tesla and smashed bank windows, channelling anger at what they called concentrated political and economic power. The march came days after Tesla's owner, Elon Musk, became the world's first trillionaire — a milestone that protesters cited as a symbol of rising inequality.

France deployed 16,000 law enforcement officers to secure the summit, an operation that officials compared in scale to the security arrangements for the 2024 Paris Olympic Games.

## What the Diaspora Should Watch

For NRIs and the broader Indian diaspora, the Evian summit is not a distant diplomatic exercise. The Iran deal's impact on oil prices flows directly into inflation, the rupee's trajectory, and the cost of remittances. The Modi-Trump bilateral will shape the visa and trade environment for Indian workers and businesses in the United States for years to come. And Macron's push to rebalance global economic imbalances — framed as "China overproduces, the United States overconsumes, Europe underinvests" — could reshape the investment landscape for India-focused funds and NRI capital flows.

The summit runs until June 17, with a leaders' dinner at the Palace of Versailles on Wednesday.
